corpus.content: 35 study records (M01..M35) on quantitative cardiac MRI in myocardial inflammation; corpus.json and corpus.md contain the same records
corpus.note: All records are fictional and were written for this evaluation; they do not describe real studies. Work only from the corpus.
corpus.citation_rule: Cite evidence only by corpus record IDs (for example [M03] in markdown and "M03" in JSON). Do not cite or name any source outside the corpus: no author-year citations, DOIs, URLs, PMIDs, arXiv IDs or 'et al.'.

technique.ECV: extracellular volume fraction (pre- and post-contrast T1 with haematocrit)

population.MYO: adults with suspected or confirmed acute myocarditis
population.ICI: patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors with suspected myocarditis
population.MULTIPLE: only for audit entries that pool several populations

reference.BX: active myocardial inflammation on endomyocardial biopsy (reference-positive = at least 14 leukocytes/mm2 including at least 7 CD3+ T lymphocytes/mm2)
reference.EVENT: prospective cardiac outcome during follow-up (cardiovascular death, heart-failure hospitalisation or sustained ventricular arrhythmia)
reference.TREAT: effect of a treatment on the MRI measure (scans before and after therapy)

definitions.examined: A record has examined a technique-population-reference combination if it reports any result relating that technique to that reference standard in that population, whatever its size or result.
definitions.underpowered: A record is underpowered if its main finding is a significant (p < 0.05) association or group difference and its smallest compared group has fewer than 15 participants (for correlation or regression analyses without groups: fewer than 30 participants in total).
definitions.replicated_finding: The same technique-population-reference association reported as significant in the same direction by at least two records that are not underpowered.
definitions.contradiction: Records that are not underpowered, examine the same technique, population and reference standard, and disagree: at least one significant and at least one null result.
definitions.dependent_record: A record whose own conclusion or rationale explicitly relies on an underpowered record by naming its record ID.
definitions.technical_success: As reported in each record's technical_success field (fraction of scanned participants with analysable measurements for that technique).

gap_rules: G1 The proposed primary question relates one MRI technique (technique code) in one patient population (population code other than HV and MULTIPLE) to one reference standard (BX or EVENT).
G2 Not examined: no corpus record has examined that combination.

G3 Validated elsewhere: in at least one other population a record that is not underpowered found a significant association of that technique with that reference standard, and that technique-reference association is not the subject of a contradiction in any population.
G4 Technically feasible in the target population: a corpus record reports technical success >= 85% for that technique in the target population.
G5 Reference obtainable: a corpus record reports that reference standard obtained in the target population.
G6 The proposal must not rely on any record you flag as underpowered.

controls_vocabulary.blinded_image_analysis: MRI measurements made blinded to the reference standard
controls_vocabulary.exercise_abstinence_before_mri: no strenuous exercise for a fixed period before MRI
controls_vocabulary.corticosteroid_timing_control: MRI before high-dose corticosteroid treatment, or record and adjust for treatment timing, where the corpus shows that treatment changes the MRI measure independently of the reference standard
controls_vocabulary.fixed_field_strength_and_sequence: all MRI with one field strength and one sequence for the primary measure; no pooling across protocols
controls_vocabulary.mri_close_in_time_to_reference: MRI within a short prespecified interval of the reference standard
controls_vocabulary.consecutive_recruitment: consecutive recruitment without selection on the reference result
controls_vocabulary.blood_pool_excluded_roi_placement: measure in mid-wall myocardial regions of interest that exclude the blood pool and epicardial fat
controls_vocabulary.free_breathing_or_motion_corrected_acqui: use a free-breathing, respiratory-triggered or motion-corrected acquisition
controls_vocabulary.sedation_protocol: sedate participants who cannot stay still
controls_vocabulary.repeat_mri_subset: repeat MRI in a subset to estimate repeatability

sample_size_rules.analysis: two-sided comparison of the mean of the primary MRI measure between two independent groups defined by the reference standard (reference-positive vs reference-negative)
sample_size_rules.formula: n_per_group = ceil(2 * (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{power})^2 * SD^2 / Delta^2) (normal approximation, equal group sizes)
sample_size_rules.inputs: Delta (target difference) must be a between-group difference reported by corpus records that are not underpowered and that related the same technique to the same reference standard (one record's value or a combination of such records). SD must be a within-group or between-subject SD reported by such records or by a record that measured the same technique in the target population. List the record IDs used.
sample_size_rules.recruitment: Prospective consecutive recruitment from the target population without selection on the reference result. smaller_group_fraction = expected fraction of evaluable participants in the smaller reference-defined group, from corpus records in the target population. nonevaluable_fraction = expected fraction of recruited participants without an evaluable MRI measurement or an evaluable reference standard, from corpus records in the target population; combine independent sources as 1 - prod(1 - p_i). n_total_to_enrol = ceil(n_per_group / (smaller_group_fraction * (1 - nonevaluable_fraction))).

evidence_audit.replicated_findings: list of {technique, population, reference (codes), record_ids: [..], finding: string}; every replicated finding in the corpus per the definition
evidence_audit.contradictions: list of {technique, population, reference, significant_record_ids: [..], null_record_ids: [..], explaining_factor: one value of explaining_factor_vocabulary, explanation: string, explanation_support_ids: [..] (optional)}
evidence_audit.underpowered_claims: list of {record_id, dependent_record_ids: [..], reason: string}; every underpowered record per the definition

proposal_json_schema.gap: {technique, population, reference (codes), statement: string, supporting_record_ids: [..] (records that establish G3, G4 and G5)}
proposal_json_schema.hypothesis: {statement: string, direction: 'higher' or 'lower' (primary MRI measure in the reference-positive group relative to the reference-negative group)}
proposal_json_schema.primary_endpoint: {name, technique (code), unit, definition (how and where it is measured), reference (code), reference_positive_definition}
proposal_json_schema.design: {type, unit_of_analysis, recruitment (values from design_vocabulary), description: string}
proposal_json_schema.sample_size: {alpha, power, sided, target_difference, target_difference_source_ids: [..], sd, sd_source_ids: [..], n_per_group (integer), smaller_group_fraction, smaller_group_fraction_source_ids: [..], nonevaluable_fraction, nonevaluable_fraction_source_ids: [..], n_total_to_enrol (integer), formula: string}
proposal_json_schema.controls: list of {code (from controls_vocabulary), record_ids: [..] (corpus records that motivate it; [] if none), justification: string}
proposal_json_schema.risks: list of at least two {risk, mitigation}

proposal_md_requirements: Sections for the evidence audit, gap, hypothesis, primary endpoint, design, sample size, controls, risks and limitations.
Cite records as [Mxx]; every record in gap.supporting_record_ids must be cited in the markdown.
State n_per_group and n_total_to_enrol as numbers matching proposal.json.
grading_note: Deterministic automated checks of proposal.json and proposal.md against the corpus and the rules above: schema and vocabularies, record IDs and external citations, evidence-audit sets, the gap and its support, endpoint and design choices, sample-size inputs and arithmetic, controls and their supporting records, and the markdown. Deliverables are read from the workspace root or one subfolder.
